Right, thank you. This has been a really thorough survey – quite dense, actually! I found Q3.5, specifically regarding sensitive data like disability and race/ethnicity, incredibly difficult. The “never” response was pretty unanimous, which makes sense given my role as an advisor; disclosing that information feels… profoundly intrusive. 

The most important thing for me is Q3.2 – using course performance data. Small improvement is the bare minimum I’d accept. It seems logical to leverage existing student records to identify struggles early. However, the scale of the “large” responses on Absalon activity data worries me - that feels like a huge privacy risk and frankly, unnecessary complexity. 

The biggest divergence appears around Q5.2 – prioritising equal recall versus fairness. While I understand both perspectives, I think aiming for *both* is crucial; we can’t simply sacrifice accuracy for equity. Perhaps an opt-out system could be implemented alongside the model to address concerns about over-identification?
